generated_summary: `ca` must be the primary CAPRMEDIO Main Skill entry point for Operators and AI Agents to request methodology-defined Workflows and exchange current MCP Step instructions and results.
PROGRAMMATIC owns all and only deterministic behavior of FRAMEWORK_ENGINE.
Preserve all information needed for intended use; expose only the complete, currently justified set needed for the task, and retain the rest for retrieval.
Apply DRY (Don’t repeat yourself) when operating the Project.
GRAPH_UI owns the optional human-facing interface over GRAPH_SERVER and must not be required for headless graph access, Tools, or MCP.
FIELD must collect feedback, questions, suggestions, and problem reports from other CAPRMEDIO users.
COMMUNITY_EXTENSIONS must catalog externally maintained Extension packages without making them CAPRMEDIO-owned Scope Units.

On the existing MCP HTTP Gateway, `/health` must provide an explicit HTML browser view of bounded, safe, process-local health, Tool-call, and Workflow observations while preserving existing machine JSON `ready` and readiness-status semantics. It is non-authoritative and read-only: use actual observed calls and results only, keep scheduler status separate, cap each history at 32, hide and escape sensitive data, and never trigger, replay, mutate, or infer successful execution from liveness or absent observations.

Code Candidate Semantic Review is a read-only Action that checks a candidate against actual Evaluation and diagnosis evidence plus selected current R/M/E/D and Project-owned Tier 0 bindings, reusing applicable Method-policy obligations without creating policy. Its result is `passed`, `findings`, `partial`, `unresolved`, or, in preliminary phase, `preliminary_clear` only under the defined evidence and completeness rules; it performs no fixes, edits, retries, promotion, release, or Journal-completeness gate.

Shared Implementation Review Step must invoke exactly one `CA-O-238-PROJECT_CONFIGURATION-ACTION--review-code-candidate-evidence-and-applicable-method-policy-without-editing` Action in explicit Integrated context, with an explicit preliminary or final `review_phase` and source-bound project, candidate, policy, evidence, input, permission, and retry-state bindings. It passes the review result directly to the enclosing Workflow and remains read-only, preserving revisions, bindings, findings, effects, and results without editing, retrying, or launching release.

The Evaluation must verify RMEDO Conflict Resolution and its reused Actions against CA-O-028-PROJECT_CONFIGURATION-WORKFLOW--resolve-rmedo-conflicts-without-leaving-gaps without losing authority, using exact source Revisions before and after correction. Preserve higher-tier authority, prefer a newer aligned same-tier Claim, report uncertainty instead of inventing a winner, and archive only when coverage, alignment, authorization, and conflict checks pass; otherwise block or ask the Operator and report actual effects.

An Operator-authorized RMED Atoms Base Revise Run must produce a full traceable record, including partial, blocked, and empty Runs, in both its Markdown report and correlated shared Project Journal Records. The report retains scope, source and rule bindings, per-Atom evidence, findings, dispositions, pending work, blockers, and outcome; the Journal records actual Events with the same Run ID and report reference, and recording failures remain explicit.
The CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance must keep all valuable Project information recoverable across sessions, handoffs, context loss, and Implementation changes.

The Project-wide foundation and Core set Evaluation must return `fail` for missing canonical ownership, narrow foundational commitments, missing required Core Claims, conflicting or duplicate authority in one context, or incompatible Local Tier or Content Role. It may return `pass` only for the reviewed frontier, must assess each foundational commitment's complete primary contribution against its Content Role, and must report missing or conflicting owners to the Operator without silently choosing a winner.

MCP must own the provider-neutral discovery, schema, and dispatch interface for invoking active CAPRMEDIO Tools, receiving ACTION_PROMPTS or OPERATOR_PROMPTS, and starting or resuming Workflows. It must not own Tool behavior, Prompt content, Workflow coordination, Skill procedures, application behavior, or agent-host-specific packaging.

YAML Frontmatter of a Markdown Atom Carrier must use the least syntax and nesting that still provides deterministic parsing, validation, extensibility, and human readability, with governed field encodings and cardinalities; Summary and Claim remain body sections, and unadmitted or filename-derived values are invalid. Drafts, including the source-pinned Subjects-only edit draft, must follow their governed IDs, status, filenames, canonical-source protection, approval, and history rules; new fields require authority for their location, type, cardinality, admission, and values or references.
The Project has exactly five ordered Layers: FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY (1), FRAMEWORK_ENGINE (2), OPERATOR_DOCUMENTATION (3), CORE_EXTENSIONS (4), and RELEASES (5).

PROMPTS must own prompt-based implementations used by an AI Agent or presented to the Operator; the implemented methodology Action, Workflow, decision authority, and programmatic mechanics remain with their existing owners.
The caprmedio Project must create and evolve a working CAPRMEDIO Framework that lets any Operator use AI Agents to create, deliver, run, and maintain any feasible Project.

For each selected Scope, check every active Atom, including Methodology source Atoms, against every active Project-wide foundational invariant before applying lower-tier authority. Pass only when there are no conflicts or overrides; report and route all conflicts as specified.
Every CAPRMEDIO Feature is an `unordered_unit`, has exactly one immediate Structural unit owner, and has no `local_order`.
The CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance and AI Agents must communicate with the Operator as much as needed, but no more than needed, for informed decisions.

The CAPRMEDIO Framework includes all caprmedio Project outputs delivered to the repository's root Implementation Folders. OPERATOR_DOCUMENTATION, CORE_EXTENSIONS, and RELEASES are downstream Project Layers; COMMUNITY_EXTENSIONS and FIELD are direct Project Features.
The CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance and the Implementation must form one connected Graph of Graphs.
When applying the Applicable Methodology, FRAMEWORK_ENGINE must minimize token consumption, AI Agent mistakes, and irrelevant or stale context while preserving required Project outcomes.
CORE_EXTENSIONS must provide CAPRMEDIO-maintained Extensions that add or specialize optional capabilities without changing canonical Core Meta-Model authority.
OPERATOR_DOCUMENTATION must give the Operator enough readable information to use a CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance efficiently and achieve their Project Goals.

The CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance must not require any of the Operator's human participants to gain specialist craft proficiency or personally perform specialist craft work to create, deliver, run, or maintain any feasible Project.
Every Project Layer is an immediate child of CAPRMEDIO and does not own another Project Layer's scope.
The CAPRMEDIO Framework Instance must support Configuration of available capabilities and adding new capabilities through Extensions.

CAPRMEDIO must help the Operator produce and evaluate an improvement proposal for every material observed Project outcome, limited to the narrowest affected scope and the Operator's current authority.
FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY must define how Projects are represented and operated.
RELEASES must provide usable, evaluated CAPRMEDIO versions with release notes covering changes, compatibility, and known limitations.

FRAMEWORK_ENGINE must provide enough observability and transparency for the Operator to understand execution, inspect changes and evidence, recognize failures and limitations, and make informed decisions.
For a complete decomposition of a declared whole at one level, apply MECE.
To govern the Project, keep Terms, Claims, rules, structure, and Implementation mutually coherent wherever they share authority or interact.
To govern the Project's mechanisms, admit or retain a mechanism only when other admitted mechanisms cannot preserve a required outcome or material governed distinction.
Governed commitments and results must be checkable when they are used to govern work or evaluate a result.
